records.etiology_en:
Nocturnal frequency/polyuria has indeed troubled the Chinese for more than a thousand years. As early as around 600 CE, the classical text Zhu Bing Yuan Hou Lun (Treatise on the Origins and Manifestations of the Various Diseases) clearly recorded: 'Copious, uninhibited urination arises from Bladder Deficiency-Cold and slipperiness of the bladder. The Kidney is the zang; the Bladder is the fu of the Kidney; as exterior and interior they both govern water. Kidney Qi passes downward to the genitals; since the fu is Deficient-Cold and cannot warm its zang, the urine is white and copious; and when nocturia is especially severe, it is because internal Yin Qi is arising.'

The meaning of this passage is that frequent urination is caused by 'Bladder Deficiency-Cold.' The Bladder is the organ attached to the Kidney; the two stand in an interior-exterior relationship, and both govern water.

Kidney Qi travels downward to the genital region; since the Bladder is Deficient-Cold, it cannot warm the Kidney, so the urine is white and copious. If nocturia is especially heavy, it is because the internal 'Yin-Cold Qi' is exuberant.

Thus the ancients held that Bladder Deficiency-Cold denotes insufficiency of the Bladder's Yang Qi, which leads to urination that is hard to control and therefore frequent. Nocturia is especially heavy because Yang Qi is weaker at night and the Bladder is more easily affected by Cold.

The ancients held that Yin-Cold of the Kidney and Bladder is the cause of urinary frequency.

The following are some common symptoms of frequent urination:

A marked increase in the number of urinations, with frequent trips to the toilet both day and night.

A relatively small urine volume, with clear, transparent urine.

Urination that is hard to control, with a tendency to urinary incontinence.

A cold sensation in the lower abdomen, with lumbar soreness and back pain.

On this basis, nearly all Chinese physicians of later generations have continued to use this concept when diagnosing nocturnal frequency. The Kidney governs Water and controls opening and closing, while the Bladder governs the storage of urine; hence nocturnal polyuria is inseparable from the Kidney and Bladder of Chinese medicine.

Daytime is 'Yang' and nighttime is 'Yin'; at night Yin flourishes and Yang wanes. Nocturnal polyuria is therefore the result of weak Yang Qi.

Explained in a single sentence: frequency/polyuria, whether by day or by night, is caused by insufficiency of the Yang Qi of the Kidney and Bladder.

In November 2023 a member shared that after autumn and winter arrived, the frequency of his nighttime urination clearly increased: previously only once a night, it now reached twice, each time with a large urine volume of clear, transparent urine — even though he had not drunk much water before bed.

Having performed meridian testing on himself for 3 years, he had confirmed that he belongs to the 'Cold-type Yang-Deficient meridian constitution,' and it is like this every year when winter comes.

He said: 'Actually it is not only in winter. Even in summer, as long as I stay in an air-conditioned room where the temperature is too low, I immediately become very frequent, especially from the afternoon onward.'

The so-called 'Cold-type Yang-Deficient meridian constitution' commonly presents Deficiency of the Gallbladder, Stomach, and Kidney channels, or Gallbladder plus Kidney channel Deficiency, just as in the figure below — this is the meridian pattern most prone to frequency/nocturia.

The most common meridian pattern of the Yang-Deficient constitution.

From the figure above it is easy to see that in cold weather — that is, when the temperature drops — the probability of this meridian pattern appearing rises, fully corroborating the ancient theory of Chinese medicine.

So even without performing meridian testing on oneself, this meridian phenomenon appears in most people, which is why the probability of frequency/nocturia in winter is higher than in summer.

Besides this Yang-Deficient meridian pattern, another common pattern, the 'Iron Triangle,' can also produce frequency/nocturia.

One member who observed her own meridians long-term confirmed that she belongs to the 'Iron Triangle' meridian constitution; she experienced frequency/nocturia nearly every night, which often affected her sleep.

A large proportion of people with the Iron Triangle meridian pattern very readily show the phenomenon of 'Kidney channel Deficiency.' This meridian pattern consists of Spleen channel Deficiency together with Kidney and Bladder channel Deficiency — which of course means insufficient Kidney/Bladder Qi and Blood, no less serious than the Yang-Deficient meridian phenomenon.

The Iron Triangle meridian pattern can also present Kidney channel Deficiency.

This is why the ancient Chinese physicians discovered that 'Liver constraint with Blood Deficiency,' 'Spleen Deficiency with exuberant Dampness,' 'Liver-Kidney insufficiency,' 'Heart-Spleen dual Deficiency,' 'Spleen-Kidney dual Deficiency,' and the like can also cause frequency/nocturia — something meridian data can fully corroborate.

Accordingly, the treatment methods for improving nocturia begin to grow complicated: it is no longer as simple as treating only 'Kidney Deficiency' or 'Cold'!

A certain proportion of people have a meridian constitution tending toward the 'composite meridian constitution' — some Iron Triangle features plus some Cold — so Kidney channel Deficiency is a certainty, and they can hardly escape the trouble of frequency.

People with nocturia usually also have other concurrent symptoms, for example: dizziness, depression and fatigue, tinnitus, hearing impairment, lumbar soreness and back pain, seminal emission, premature ejaculation, knee pain, diarrhea, cold limbs, poor appetite, and so on.

Whatever the cause of the Kidney Deficiency, proper health cultivation that raises the energy of the Kidney channel will improve nocturia symptoms. For those with heavy internal Cold, simply expelling the Cold, boosting the body's Yang Qi, and keeping the body warm will improve frequency/nocturia.

Those who overuse their brains, are excessively fatigued, or are under too much stress should start with relaxing body, mind, and spirit, combined with taking some Chinese herbs that harmonize the Liver, Spleen, and Kidney, which can fundamentally improve frequency/nocturia.

Once one finds one's own cause and cultivates health accordingly to improve the abnormal meridians, long-troubling frequency/nocturia will improve — everyone can verify this personally.

註1: 耳脈為早期經脈名，即手少陽經，出自馬王堆漢墓帛書，書上記載：「耳溫（脈）：起于手北（背），出臂外兩骨之間，[上骨]下廉，[出肘中]，入耳中。是動則病：耳聾，煇煇朜朜，嗌種（腫）。是耳脈主治其所產病：目外漬（眥）痛，頰痛，耳聾，為三病。」文中所載的內容與《黃帝內經靈樞·經脈》之手少陽經類似。

註2: 耳鳴的辨證有：風熱襲肺、肝火上炎、肝陽上亢、肝血不足、腎陰虛、腎氣不足、心腎不交、脾胃虛弱、痰火、氣滯血瘀…等等，可見外感六邪與五臟六腑不平衡都會造成耳鳴，可以改善的中藥非常多。可以改善耳鳴的中藥很多，例如：桑菊飲、當歸龍薈丸、天麻鉤藤飲、逍遙散、四物湯、耳聾左慈丸、天王補心丹、交泰丸、補中益氣湯、二陳湯、通竅活血湯…等等至少上百種中藥。

《雜病源流犀燭》：「耳聾者，音聲閉隔，竟一無所聞者也，亦有不至無聞，但聞之不真者，名為重聽。」

records.etiology_zh:
耳鳴絕對是是困擾中國人千年以上的症狀，古代中醫典籍經常一起探討耳鳴與耳聾，因為這兩種疾病背後的原因是一樣的。

古書《外科證治全書》就提到：「耳鳴者，耳中有聲，或若嬋鳴，或若鐘鳴，或若火熇熇然，或若流水聲，或若簸米聲，或睡著如打戰鼓，如風入耳。」

若從中醫的證候探討耳鳴，可能性非常多，至少有十幾種可能性。而最簡單的下手處，就是先從通過耳朵的經絡開始下手研究。

講到耳朵，首先最重要的經絡就是「三焦經」，在古代被稱為「耳脈」，所以很明顯，古人認為耳朵的疾病，一定與三焦經有關聯。

除了三焦經，依照經絡專家藺雲桂的《經絡圖解》一書中所述，通往耳部的經絡還有膽經、膀胱經、小腸經、胃經、腎經、大腸經絡脈，總共6條經脈，1條絡脈。可見通往耳朵的經絡非常複雜。

通往耳朵的經絡總共6條經脈，1條絡脈

耳脈就是三焦經嗎？許多人不知道這件事，也無法理解什麼是三焦經？

雲端醫某會員K先生就曾分享，他長期觀察自己的身體與經絡的關係，每次只要感到火氣大時，無名指指甲旁邊「關衝穴」附近就會疼痛，耳鳴會短暫出現30秒然後迅速消失，只要將關衝穴放血，釋放過多的火氣後，耳鳴的現象就會不見，屢試不爽。

另一位會員長期在國外執業的針灸師，她也分享：「每次只要病患出現耳朵不舒服症狀，像耳朵塞住、耳鳴、耳朵痛…等，只要針灸三焦經上的中渚穴、液門穴、翳風穴，都可以快速改善！」可見三焦經與耳朵是息息相關的。

從古至今中醫治療耳鳴的方法很多，因此產生很多證候辨證，非常複雜，若將這些辨證統計起來至少十幾種(見下圖)，看起來令人眼花撩亂。學習中醫者如果看到以下的分類，可能就會認為自己永遠都學不會了！

耳鳴/耳聾/耳朵痛的中醫證型相當複雜

不論造成耳鳴的中醫證候有幾百種，治療的中藥幾百種，背後的經絡型態卻最多只有3-5種，所以完全可以「化繁完簡」，一點都不難學！在此歸納出一些簡單的經絡型態：

一、一派陽虛經絡型態

當一個人屬於陽虛體質時，代表體內很寒，出現的經絡型態經常會出現下圖的狀態：肝經、膽經、胃經與腎經虛證，三焦經與大腸經也會出現虛證。

簡單說，這種經絡型態的少陽經、陽明經都是虛證，可以說通往耳朵的部位，一年四季都處於經絡不暢通的狀態，所以久了之後很容易出現耳鳴。

這種經絡型態，許多人過去看不懂，現在只要開啟3D模式，就可以很輕易理解了，從下圖可以看到，通往耳朵附近的經絡都是藍色的，這就是一種阻塞的現象。

一派陽虛經絡型態最容易出現耳鳴

這種經絡型態很容易出現在寒冷的冬天，很有機會出現「肝血虛」、「腎陰虛」、「腎陽虛」、「心腎不交」這類證候，都有可能出現耳鳴，伴隨其他症狀。

這種經絡型態，肝經虛證，肝藏血的功能失職。而腎經幾乎一年四季都出現虛證，在《黃帝內經》上提到：「腎氣通於耳，腎和則耳能聞五音矣。五臟不和則七竅不通」所以耳朵一定不會正常。

拋開這些證候，若直接從經絡理解比較直接，這些經絡不是全部都通過耳朵嗎？這些通過耳朵的經絡都因為氣血不足，當然會出現耳鳴或聽力衰退了！只要提升這些氣血不足的經絡能，耳鳴就會改善。

運用中藥也可以疏通經絡，某位會員在2020年時就分享，她出現耳鳴、耳朵痛，連喉嚨脖子都在痛，她就吃了一次「麻黃附子細辛湯」科學中藥，沒想到喉嚨痛與耳朵痛都好了。

2022年時有一位會員也分享，他在進入冬天之後，偶爾就會出現耳鳴，由於他就是這種經絡型態，所以他去買了一台遠紅外線照射機器，除了溫熱腳部之外，也溫熱手部與側邊頭部，感覺改善效果很明顯，之前手腳冰冷的現象也改善了。[@ad:1]

二、鐵三角經絡型態的變化型

耳鳴的人如果去看中醫的話，通常醫生會說這是體內火熱的現象，所以耳鳴在中醫常常會被診斷為「熱證」，這個方向是沒錯的，運用經絡數據也可以印證這件事。

上面提到的體內寒氣過重的經絡現象，最多也只會出現在30%-40%的人身上，不是每個人體內都是寒的，有一定比例的人體內會是熱的。

尤其是鐵三角經絡型態，最容易出現熱證。當鐵三角經絡型態持續一段時間之後，很容易出現極熱的現象，也就是下圖的經絡型態：體內少陽經(三焦經、膽經)、陽明經(胃經、大腸經)都是實證，肝經也是實證，而脾經與膀胱經出現虛證。

鐵三角經絡型態變化型容易出現耳鳴

從上圖可以輕易看出，耳朵附近的經絡都是紅色的，一副就是很火熱的狀態，這更容易出現耳鳴。

這種經絡型態很容易出現在炎熱夏天，因此夏天的「風熱」感冒也會出現類似的經絡現象。這種經絡型態，還可能出現「肝火上炎」、「肝陽上亢」、「膽火胃火熾盛」體內火毒熾盛...等等證候，伴隨其他各種症狀。

雲端中醫某會員在2020年7月時就分享，當時她出現耳鳴及耳朵痛，剛開始1-2天才出現一次，很快就消失。漸漸地每天都會出現1次，到8月的時候每天出現3-5次，讓她感到很不舒服。這段期間她經常頭暈、胸口發熱、容易生氣、口乾舌燥、便秘、晚上睡不好、胃口不好經常吃不下...等等。

通往耳朵的經絡異常，造成耳鳴耳朵痛

從圖上可以看出，她的經絡圖就是夏天常見的經絡型態，有一定機率會出現耳鳴現象。然而，這種經絡型態在一年四季都可以出現，那就是熬夜與工作壓力大。

2022年冬天12月時，有一位新進會員透過FB社團分享，他在12月初至今連續檢測兩個星期，檢測的經絡圖都很類似，是膽經幾乎每天都是實證。

他最困擾的就是右耳高頻耳鳴約1年多，而且右邊下巴淋巴異常，右下巴後方的臉頰也會酸酸的，而這些全部都位於膽經的路線上。

男性右耳出現高頻耳鳴持一年多的經絡型態

這種經絡型態其實很有可能也屬於這種鐵三角經絡型態的變化型，因為在冬天檢測反而被隱藏起來了，只要持續觀察到隔年5-6月，通常就會出現典型的鐵三角經絡型態現象。

由於這種經絡型態相當難解，出現的疾病更不只有耳鳴，雲端中醫曾經歸納出一篇文章(點選閱讀)，並提出相關的解決方案(點選閱讀)。

其實，大家只要到網路上去Google，多了解一些長期耳鳴的人分享出來的經驗，都會找到共同的特點。例如：很喜歡熬夜、工作壓力非常大、工作細節忙碌、脾氣不好很容易生氣、個性太龜毛、緊張兮兮、神經質整天處於被害妄想狀態…等等，可見過度「疲勞累積」與「情緒不佳」是造成耳鳴最典型的原因！

許多人在熬夜的時候，耳鳴就會自動跑出來，這時候如果你當場幫自己進行經絡檢測，就會看到類似的經絡型態。本篇文章在第一次發表時，阿編就是在深夜寫到一半出現耳鳴，趕快跑去睡覺，明天再寫。

三、脾胃虛弱

上面的兩種經絡型態，其實已經完全解釋了造成耳鳴的兩種極端的經絡型態，一般人不會出現這麼嚴重的狀態。

以上兩種型態不論是哪一種，都容易會出現「脾胃虛弱」證候，這時候也很容易出現耳鳴。這是因為脾胃為氣血生化之源，脾胃虛弱或脾陽不振時，清氣不能上升，濁陰阻滯耳部經脈而出現耳朵疾病。

同時，由於脾主運化，脾胃虛弱的人體內容易水液運化不良而生痰，中醫認為「痰火」也會造成耳鳴。全身出現沈重、頭昏，胸悶、咳嗽痰多，阻滯耳朵的氣血。

脾胃虛弱可以說是過去兩千年來，中醫最常辨證的一種證候，絕大多數的疾病也是源自於此。

因為體內血液、水液循環不良所造成的耳鳴也常見，例如就有一位設計師，就因為趴在桌上睡覺就造成右耳全聾，醫生診斷認為是他習慣性把咖啡當水分補充，時間一久之後血液變濃稠，導致耳朵旁的血管堵塞，造成耳朵中風。

從經絡角度來看，通過耳朵的經絡不只有三焦經，以膽經、三焦經、小腸經、大腸經與胃經為例，都是與脾胃消化系統有關，所以脾胃虛弱時出現耳鳴也不令人意外了！

四、氣滯血瘀與肥胖

不論哪一種經絡型態的耳鳴，其實都不是重點，因為慢性耳鳴通常就是某些經絡長期氣血不通所造成，所以只要疏通相關的經絡、肌肉沾粘、血管阻塞...等等，就可以緩解耳鳴。

簡單說，當一個人長期出現某一種「經絡型態」，成為一種「經絡體質」之後，代表著體內長期某些經絡阻塞不通，累積很久之後就會全身氣滯血瘀，一定比例的人就會出現難治性的耳鳴。

由於這種經絡阻塞一定要累積一段至少數年，甚至數十年的時間，所以這種慢性耳鳴通常是出現在中老年人的身上，年輕人比較不會出現。

長期氣血經絡阻塞之後，一定會出現經筋病變，可以運用現代很流行的肌筋膜激痛點療法，找出沾粘的肌肉，揉開之後就會改善。同時也要去檢查是否「頸椎」已經出現病變，壓迫到神經而造成耳鳴。

頭面部、頸部與背部的經肌肉頸椎都會影響到耳朵

台灣耳鳴學會理事長賴仁淙提出，肥胖也是造成耳鳴的主要原因，他分享中國大陸有一名專門治療耳鳴的中醫師，治療的秘訣就是「吃素」與「10點前就寢」，不碰動物性脂肪與睡眠充足，發胖的可能性自然比較小，可以成功控制體重，改善耳鳴。

多數的時候，耳朵的問題都可以透過經絡或物理療法(針灸按摩穴道、推拿相關肌肉、調整脊椎…等等)，改善生活習慣或是釋放壓力來改善，甚至痊癒，只要方法正確就一點也不難。

簡單歸納一句話：如果一個人長期養生，保持全身經絡暢通，且持續放鬆心情的話，是幾乎不太可能出現耳鳴的，就算出現了也很快便可以痊癒。
records.western_pathology_zh:
所謂的「耳」，是指當耳朵在外在環境沒發出聲音，卻能感受到噪音(鈴響聲、輕敲聲、蟬鳴聲或低吼聲...等等)。由於耳鳴的患者經常出現聽力缺損，因此「耳鳴」與「耳聾」經常一起被討論。

依照統計，在美國有超過4,500萬人受到耳鳴的困擾，全人類中大約有15%的人受到耳鳴的困擾。隨時間過去，耳鳴常常會越來越嚴重。

有些耳鳴者會因此情緒低落、焦慮或難以集中精神。有10%的人是因為糖尿病引起耳鳴，1%的人終其一生長期受到耳鳴的困擾，這聽起來是相當恐怖的事。

耳鳴並不是一種疾病，而是許多原因的的症狀。造成耳鳴的原因非常多，例如：外傷、耳垢阻塞、鼓膜穿孔、噪音性損傷…等等，都有可能出現耳鳴。

有些疾病會出現耳鳴，例如：糖尿病、顏面神經麻痺、病毒感染帶狀皰疹、心血管疾病、美尼爾氏綜合症、鼻竇炎、鼻咽癌、憂鬱症、中耳炎、腦中風、腦部腫瘤聽神經瘤...等等。

有些人聽到的是血管的聲音，或是耳朵附近的肌肉沾粘產生耳朵塞住感的耳鳴，原因實在太複雜了。

然而，一定比例的人並沒有被診斷出其他疾病，卻出現單純的耳鳴，進行各種檢查依然成因不明。這時候就可以運用神秘的中醫經絡來加以解釋，提供一條不同的思路。

註1: 耳脈為早期經脈名，即手少陽經，出自馬王堆漢墓帛書，書上記載：「耳溫（脈）：起于手北（背），出臂外兩骨之間，[上骨]下廉，[出肘中]，入耳中。是動則病：耳聾，煇煇朜朜，嗌種（腫）。是耳脈主治其所產病：目外漬（眥）痛，頰痛，耳聾，為三病。」文中所載的內容與《黃帝內經靈樞·經脈》之手少陽經類似。

註2: 耳鳴的辨證有：風熱襲肺、肝火上炎、肝陽上亢、肝血不足、腎陰虛、腎氣不足、心腎不交、脾胃虛弱、痰火、氣滯血瘀…等等，可見外感六邪與五臟六腑不平衡都會造成耳鳴，可以改善的中藥非常多。可以改善耳鳴的中藥很多，例如：桑菊飲、當歸龍薈丸、天麻鉤藤飲、逍遙散、四物湯、耳聾左慈丸、天王補心丹、交泰丸、補中益氣湯、二陳湯、通竅活血湯…等等至少上百種中藥。

《雜病源流犀燭》：「耳聾者，音聲閉隔，竟一無所聞者也，亦有不至無聞，但聞之不真者，名為重聽。」
records.western_pathology_en:
So-called 'tinnitus' refers to perceiving noise (ringing, light tapping, cicada-like chirping, low roaring, and so on) when the external environment is producing no sound. Because tinnitus patients frequently present hearing deficits, 'tinnitus' and 'deafness' are often discussed together.

According to statistics, more than 45 million people in the United States are troubled by tinnitus, and roughly 15% of all humanity is affected by it. As time passes, tinnitus often becomes progressively worse.

Some tinnitus sufferers consequently become low in mood, anxious, or unable to concentrate. In 10% of people the tinnitus is caused by diabetes, and 1% are troubled by chronic tinnitus for their entire lives — which sounds like a rather terrifying prospect.

Tinnitus is not a disease in itself but a symptom with many causes. The causes of tinnitus are very numerous, for example: trauma, earwax impaction, tympanic membrane perforation, noise-induced injury, and so on can all produce tinnitus.

Certain diseases can present with tinnitus, for example: diabetes, facial nerve palsy, herpes zoster viral infection, cardiovascular disease, Meniere's disease, sinusitis, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, depression, otitis media, stroke, and brain tumors such as acoustic neuroma, among others.

Some people hear the sound of their own blood vessels, or have tinnitus with a blocked-ear sensation produced by adhesions of the muscles near the ear — the causes are simply too complex.

Nevertheless, a certain proportion of people are diagnosed with no other disease yet present simple tinnitus, and the cause remains unknown despite every kind of examination. At this point the mysterious meridians of Chinese medicine can be applied to explain it, providing a different line of thinking.

records.etiology_en:
Tinnitus has unquestionably troubled the Chinese for more than a thousand years. Ancient Chinese medical texts frequently discuss tinnitus and deafness together, because the causes underlying these two conditions are the same.

The ancient text Wai Ke Zheng Zhi Quan Shu (Complete Book of Patterns and Treatments in External Medicine) states: 'In tinnitus there is sound within the ear — sometimes like the chirping of cicadas, sometimes like the tolling of a bell, sometimes like the crackling of fire, sometimes like the sound of flowing water, sometimes like the winnowing of rice; or, when asleep, like the beating of war drums, like wind entering the ear.'

If tinnitus is examined through Chinese medical patterns, the possibilities are very numerous — at least a dozen or more. The simplest starting point is to begin by studying the meridians that pass through the ear.

Speaking of the ear, the first and most important meridian is the Triple Burner (San Jiao) channel, called the 'ear vessel' in antiquity — so it is evident that the ancients considered diseases of the ear necessarily linked to the Triple Burner channel.

Besides the Triple Burner channel, according to the meridian expert Lin Yun-Gui's Illustrated Guide to the Meridians, the channels reaching the ear also include the Gallbladder, Bladder, Small Intestine, Stomach, and Kidney channels and the Large Intestine luo-vessel — six channels and one collateral in all. Clearly the meridians reaching the ear are very complex.

Six channels and one collateral reach the ear in all.

Is the ear vessel really the Triple Burner channel? Many people do not know this, nor can they understand what the Triple Burner channel is.

Mr. K, a Cloud TCM member, once shared that through long-term observation of the relationship between his body and his meridians, whenever he feels internal Fire flaring, the area near Guanchong (TB-1) beside the ring-finger nail becomes painful, and tinnitus appears briefly for about 30 seconds before quickly disappearing; simply bloodletting at Guanchong to release the excess Fire makes the tinnitus vanish — reliably, every single time.

Another member, an acupuncturist long in practice abroad, also shared: 'Whenever a patient presents ear discomfort — a blocked ear, tinnitus, ear pain, and so on — needling Zhongzhu (TB-3), Yemen (TB-2), and Yifeng (TB-17) on the Triple Burner channel brings rapid improvement!' Clearly the Triple Burner channel is intimately bound up with the ear.

From antiquity to the present, Chinese medicine has had many methods of treating tinnitus, generating many pattern differentiations of great complexity; tallied up, they number at least a dozen or more (see figure below), dazzling to behold. A student of Chinese medicine who sees such a classification may well conclude that he will never be able to learn it!

The Chinese medical patterns of tinnitus/deafness/ear pain are quite complex.

Yet no matter whether the Chinese medical patterns causing tinnitus number in the hundreds, and the herbs treating it in the hundreds, the underlying meridian patterns number at most only 3-5, so the complexity can be entirely reduced to simplicity — it is not hard to learn at all! Some simple meridian patterns are summarized here:

1. The across-the-board Yang-Deficient meridian pattern

When a person has a Yang-Deficient constitution, the interior of the body is very Cold, and the meridian pattern that appears is often the state in the figure below: Deficiency of the Liver, Gallbladder, Stomach, and Kidney channels, with the Triple Burner and Large Intestine channels also showing Deficiency.

Simply put, in this meridian pattern the Shaoyang and Yangming channels are all Deficient; one can say the region leading to the ear is in a state of meridian obstruction all year round, so over time tinnitus very readily appears.

Many people previously could not read this meridian pattern; now, by simply opening 3D mode, it becomes very easy to understand. From the figure below one can see that the meridians leading to the area around the ear are all blue — a phenomenon of blockage.

The across-the-board Yang-Deficient meridian pattern most readily produces tinnitus.

This meridian pattern very readily appears in cold winter, and there is a good chance of patterns such as 'Liver Blood Deficiency,' 'Kidney Yin Deficiency,' 'Kidney Yang Deficiency,' and 'Heart-Kidney non-interaction' appearing — all of which may present tinnitus, accompanied by other symptoms.

In this meridian pattern the Liver channel is Deficient, and the Liver's function of storing Blood fails in its duty. The Kidney channel shows Deficiency in nearly all four seasons. The Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic states: 'Kidney Qi communicates with the ear; when the Kidney is in harmony, the ear can hear the five tones. When the five zang are in disharmony, the seven orifices are not free' — so the ears will certainly not be normal.

Setting these patterns aside, it is more direct to understand it straight from the meridians: do these meridians not all pass through the ear? When these ear-traversing meridians all suffer insufficiency of Qi and Blood, of course tinnitus or hearing decline appears! Simply raise the energy of these Qi-and-Blood-deficient meridians, and the tinnitus will improve.

Chinese herbs can also be used to unblock the meridians. One member shared in 2020 that she developed tinnitus and ear pain, with even her throat and neck aching; she took a single dose of Ma Huang Fu Zi Xi Xin Tang (Ephedra, Aconite and Asarum Decoction) as concentrated scientific herbal granules, and to her surprise both the sore throat and the ear pain resolved.

In 2022 another member shared that after entering winter he would occasionally develop tinnitus. Since he has exactly this meridian pattern, he bought a far-infrared radiation device and, besides warming his feet, also warmed his hands and the side of his head; he felt the improvement was very distinct, and his previous cold hands and feet improved as well. [@ad:1]

2. Variants of the Iron Triangle meridian pattern

If a person with tinnitus consults a Chinese physician, the doctor will usually say it is a phenomenon of internal Fire-Heat, so in Chinese medicine tinnitus is very often diagnosed as a 'Heat pattern.' This direction is not wrong, and meridian data can corroborate it.

The heavy internal Cold phenomenon mentioned above appears in at most 30%-40% of people; not everyone's interior is Cold — in a certain proportion of people the interior is Hot.

The Iron Triangle meridian pattern in particular most readily produces Heat patterns. Once the Iron Triangle pattern has persisted for a period, an extreme-Heat phenomenon readily appears — that is, the meridian pattern in the figure below: the Shaoyang channels (Triple Burner, Gallbladder) and the Yangming channels (Stomach, Large Intestine) are all Excess, the Liver channel is Excess as well, while the Spleen and Bladder channels show Deficiency.

The Iron Triangle variant pattern readily produces tinnitus.

From the figure above one can easily see that the meridians around the ear are all red — a picture of blazing Heat — which makes tinnitus even more likely.

This meridian pattern very readily appears in hot summer, and the 'Wind-Heat' colds of summer also present a similar meridian phenomenon. This pattern may further present 'Liver Fire flaming upward,' 'ascendant hyperactivity of Liver Yang,' 'blazing Gallbladder and Stomach Fire,' exuberant internal Fire-toxin, and other such patterns, accompanied by various other symptoms.

A Cloud TCM member shared in July 2020 that she had developed tinnitus and ear pain — at first appearing once every 1-2 days and quickly vanishing; gradually it appeared once every day, and by August 3-5 times a day, making her very uncomfortable. During this period she frequently had dizziness, heat in the chest, irritability, dry mouth and tongue, constipation, poor sleep at night, poor appetite with inability to eat, and so on.

Abnormality of the meridians leading to the ear, causing tinnitus and ear pain.

From the chart one can see that her meridian pattern is the one commonly seen in summer, which carries a certain probability of tinnitus. Yet this meridian pattern can appear in all four seasons — through staying up late and heavy work stress.

In December 2022, in winter, a new member shared through the Facebook group that he had tested continuously for two weeks since early December, and the meridian charts were all very similar, with the Gallbladder channel Excess nearly every day.

What troubled him most was high-frequency tinnitus in the right ear for over a year, along with abnormal lymph nodes at the right jaw and a sore feeling in the cheek behind the right lower jaw — all of these located along the course of the Gallbladder channel.

The meridian pattern of a man with high-frequency tinnitus of the right ear persisting over a year.

This meridian pattern may very well also be a variant of the Iron Triangle pattern, merely hidden by testing in winter; with continued observation into May-June of the following year, the typical Iron Triangle phenomenon would usually appear.

Since this meridian pattern is quite difficult to resolve, and the diseases it produces go well beyond tinnitus, Cloud TCM has previously summarized it in an article (click to read) and proposed related solutions (click to read).

In fact, if you simply Google and learn from the experiences shared by people with chronic tinnitus, you will find common features, for example: fondness for staying up late, very heavy work stress, busy detail-laden work, a bad temper with quickness to anger, an overly perfectionist personality, jumpiness, and a neurotic, almost paranoid state all day long. Clearly, accumulated 'fatigue' and 'poor emotional states' are the most typical causes of tinnitus!

In many people, tinnitus pops out of its own accord when they stay up late; if at that moment you test your own meridians on the spot, you will see a similar meridian pattern. When this article was first being written, the editor developed tinnitus while writing late into the night, hurried off to sleep, and continued the next day.

3. Spleen-Stomach weakness

The two meridian patterns above have in fact fully explained the two extreme meridian patterns behind tinnitus; ordinary people do not reach such severe states.

Whichever of the two patterns is present, however, the 'Spleen-Stomach weakness' pattern readily appears, and at that point tinnitus also readily arises. This is because the Spleen-Stomach is the source of the generation and transformation of Qi and Blood; when the Spleen-Stomach is weak or Spleen Yang fails to rouse, the clear Qi cannot ascend, and turbid Yin obstructs the channels of the ear, producing ear disease.

At the same time, since the Spleen governs transformation and transportation, in people with Spleen-Stomach weakness the body's fluids are poorly transformed and generate Phlegm; Chinese medicine holds that 'Phlegm-Fire' also causes tinnitus — with generalized heaviness, lightheadedness, chest oppression, and cough with copious phlegm, obstructing the Qi and Blood of the ear.

Spleen-Stomach weakness can be called the pattern most frequently differentiated by Chinese medicine over the past two thousand years, and the great majority of diseases also stem from it.

Tinnitus caused by poor circulation of blood and fluids in the body is also common. For example, there was a designer who went completely deaf in the right ear simply from napping face-down on his desk; the physician's diagnosis was that his habit of substituting coffee for water had, over time, thickened his blood, blocking the blood vessels beside the ear and causing a 'stroke of the ear.'

From the meridian perspective, the channels passing through the ear are not limited to the Triple Burner channel: taking the Gallbladder, Triple Burner, Small Intestine, Large Intestine, and Stomach channels as examples, all are related to the Spleen-Stomach digestive system — so the appearance of tinnitus in Spleen-Stomach weakness is no surprise either!

4. Qi stagnation with Blood stasis, and obesity

Whichever meridian pattern underlies the tinnitus is actually not the crux, because chronic tinnitus is generally produced by long-term blockage of Qi and Blood in certain meridians; so simply unblocking the relevant meridians, muscle adhesions, vascular blockages, and so on can relieve the tinnitus.

Simply put, when a person exhibits a particular 'meridian pattern' long-term and it becomes a 'meridian constitution,' it means certain meridians in the body have long been blocked and obstructed; after long accumulation, whole-body Qi stagnation with Blood stasis develops, and a certain proportion of people will develop refractory tinnitus.

Because this kind of meridian blockage must accumulate over a period of at least several years, even several decades, this chronic tinnitus usually appears in the middle-aged and elderly and is less likely to appear in the young.

After long-term blockage of Qi, Blood, and meridians, channel-sinew pathology inevitably appears; the currently popular myofascial trigger-point therapy can be applied to locate the adhered muscles, and kneading them open brings improvement. At the same time one should check whether the cervical spine has already degenerated and is compressing nerves to cause the tinnitus.

The muscles and cervical vertebrae of the head, face, neck, and back all affect the ear.

Lai Ren-Tsung, president of the Taiwan Tinnitus Society, has proposed that obesity is also a major cause of tinnitus. He shared the case of a Chinese physician in mainland China who specializes in treating tinnitus, whose secrets of treatment were 'a vegetarian diet' and 'going to bed before 10 p.m.': avoiding animal fats and getting sufficient sleep naturally lowers the likelihood of weight gain, allowing successful weight control and improvement of the tinnitus.

Most of the time, ear problems can be improved, even cured, through meridian or physical therapies (acupuncture and acupoint massage, tuina of the relevant muscles, spinal adjustment, and so on), improved lifestyle habits, or release of stress — with the correct method it is not difficult at all.

Summarized in a single sentence: if a person cultivates health long-term, keeps the meridians of the whole body unobstructed, and continually keeps the mind relaxed, it is almost impossible for tinnitus to appear; and even if it does appear, it can be cured very quickly.

records.etiology_zh:
眼睛乾澀是千年前的古人就有的症狀，古代沒有乾眼症這種名詞，但是卻有「目乾澀」這個名詞。在《黃帝內經》中有記載，名為「奪精」，《諸病源侯論》中提到：「液竭者目澀」，《證治準繩》提到「乾澀昏花」...等等。

傳統中醫認為，造成眼睛乾澀的主要原因就是「陰虧血虛」，因為《黃帝內經》中提到「五勞所傷」，第一個講的就是「久傷血」。

所以當一個人體內血虛的時候，就容易出現眼睛乾澀。然而，中醫又提到「肝藏血」、「肝開竅於目」、「脾統血」、「心主血」...等等概念，所以眼睛乾澀與中醫的心臟、脾臟與肝臟密切相關。

眼睛的淚液又屬於中醫提到的津液，當一個人體內「燥熱」時，就會出現津液不足，因此眼睛乾澀、眼睛發癢。

以上的所有內容，只要是對中醫有點興趣的人都一定看過，可謂千篇一律，陳腔濫調，抽象且沒有新義，讓人有看沒有懂，不是嗎？

如果造成眼睛乾澀的原因，可以用儀器檢測出來，運用數據化的分析來理解，這才可以讓更多現代人信服，而運用經絡檢測就可以達到此目的。

以上的分析屬於「臟腑辨證」，而運用經絡檢測屬於「經絡辨證」，要分析眼睛的疾病，首先就要探討通往眼睛的經絡有哪些？依照經絡權威藺雲桂《經絡圖解》一書上所述，通往眼睛的經絡就有15條(註1)。

若歸納這些經絡主要就是肝經、心經、膽經、胃經、小腸經、三焦經與膀胱經，這些抽象的經絡究竟是如何影響眼睛，造成眼睛乾澀的？

從一些雲端中醫的會員長期觀察之後，發現原來塑造眼睛乾燥的經絡現象，可以區分為以下3個步驟：

第一步：疲勞塑造肝經實證、膽經異常

任何人只要經常熬夜，壓力大且累積疲勞，不論有沒有大量運用眼睛，體內的肝經有很高的機率就會開始出現實證。而多數人的膽經長期虛證，經常熬夜的人，膽經會轉成實證。

熬夜過度疲勞之後，肝經膽經開始異常

基於此，任何人只要經常熬夜，體內的肝經膽經就會明顯異常，出現經絡不平衡的現象，而這兩條經絡在五行上，就是屬於「木」。

第二步：脾經膀胱經虛證

體內經絡有一個很特殊的現象是，當一個人肝經實證時，脾經與膀胱經會開始虛證。膀胱經就是起始於眼睛，當一個人體內脾經虛證時，通往面部的清陽之氣就會氣血不足，眼睛開始產生乾澀感。

肝經實證之後，脾經與膀胱經能量迅速降低

脾胃在五行就是屬「土」，體內木強就會剋土，所以脾胃虛弱。這就是為什麼，眼睛乾燥時會出現眼皮沉重或怕光現象，脾經虛證的人很容易出現眼皮的各種症狀，眼睛氣血不足時很容易怕光。

第三步：三焦經、大腸經與胃經實證

以上兩個程序，就是典型的「體三角經絡型態」，這種型態只要久了，就會出現三焦經、大腸經與胃經實證的現象，體內開始會出現一系列火熱症狀，因此眼睛會發癢發紅、口乾舌燥。這就是典型的「肝氣鬱結化熱」現象，現在可以透過數據清楚看到。

體內火氣開始出現

這就是為什麼，眼睛乾燥時通常會伴隨眼睛紅、灼熱、乾癢、異物感...就是這些經絡異常所造成的。

到了第三步的經絡現象，幾乎都是50歲以上的人長期都會出現的經絡現象，因此一個人到了50歲之後出現眼睛乾澀，就那麼理所當然了。

基於以上的分析，一個人真正要改善眼睛乾澀的現象，必須要依照以下幾個程序反向操作：

睡到飽，釋放累積疲勞：這樣肝經與膽經自然回歸正常，脾經與膀胱經不會虛證，更不會出現化熱現象。

拍打經絡，消除經筋沾粘：從上面的經絡現象看來，至少要經常拍打脾經、膀胱經與膽經，疏通這些經絡的氣血。有時候要運用抓捏的方法，在頭部、肩膀、背部附近找到激痛點，可參考下方資訊。

服用中藥或食物：如果可以配合一些「調和肝脾」、「養血養肝」的中藥或食物，自然也會有一定程度的幫助。如果體內火氣大，還要加上一些清熱解毒的中藥，輔助效果更大。

以上的分析，是從「生活習慣」所造成的經絡現象來分析的，然而像進入秋冬季節，因為外在寒氣所造成的腳三陽(膀胱經、膽經與胃經)虛證時，也容易出現眼睛乾澀，這又是另一種造成眼睛乾澀的經絡現象。

從大量現代人的經絡體質數據看來，現代人其實很容易出現眼睛乾澀、疲勞且疼痛，只要經常養生理解且改善自己的「經絡體質」，就可以從根本改善這個症狀。

註1: 通往眼睛的經絡有肝經、肝經別絡、心經、心經絡脈、心經別絡、膽經、膽經別絡、胃經、胃經別絡、陽蹺脈、陰蹺脈、任脈、小腸經、三焦經、膀胱經。

眼睛乾澀是一種現代人常見的症狀，常常會與「乾眼症」一起被討論。然而，眼睛乾澀只是短暫現象，當一個人長期眼睛乾澀就有可能是「乾眼症」，出現眼睛乾澀，卻不一定是乾眼症。

當一個人眼睛乾澀時，經常同時會出現眼睛紅、灼熱、乾癢、異物感、眼皮沉重、畏光...等等症狀。根據美國眼科學會 (AAO) 的數據顯示，50歲以上族群中，約有320萬女性和168萬男性得到乾眼症。大約有2600萬美國人感到眼睛乾澀。

造成眼睛乾澀的原因很多，最主要的原因就是用眼過多。現代人大量使用3C電腦，長時間盯著前方螢幕，一看就是7-8個小時，過度專注而不知不覺減少眨眼次數，就眼睛無法提供足夠的淚液滋潤而出現眼睛乾澀。

現代人經常是加班趕工作、熬夜使用電腦，長期待在濕度太低的環境(例如：冷氣房)，加速淚液的蒸發乾燥的環境，或是戴隱形眼鏡，都會讓眼睛乾澀。

年齡是造成眼睛乾澀的主要因素，任何只要在50歲以上的人，眼睛乾澀的狀態就會愈來愈嚴重。一些疾病如：甲狀腺疾病、糖尿病、類風濕性關節炎、乾燥症候群，也可能導致眼淚分泌減少。

在多數的時候，眼睛乾澀時只要眨眨眼流淚，或滴入乾淨的生理食鹽水後就會改善。熱敷眼睛、使用加濕器改善室內乾燥問題、多喝水補充水分、多休息，使用空氣清淨機減少空氣灰塵或汙染，都可以改善。

嚴重的乾眼症在另一篇文章中有討論。對於那些用眼不多，卻找不出原因的眼睛乾澀，這時候最適合運用中醫理論來解釋，提供一條新的思路。

records.western_pathology_en:
Dry, gritty eyes are a symptom common among modern people and are often discussed together with 'dry eye syndrome.' However, ocular dryness may be only a transient phenomenon; when a person has dry eyes long-term it may indeed be dry eye syndrome, but the appearance of dry eyes does not necessarily mean dry eye syndrome.

When a person's eyes are dry, there are often concurrent symptoms such as eye redness, burning, dry itching, foreign-body sensation, heavy eyelids, photophobia, and so on. According to data from the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO), among people over 50, about 3.2 million women and 1.68 million men have dry eye syndrome, and roughly 26 million Americans experience dry eyes.

There are many causes of dry eyes, the chief one being overuse of the eyes. Modern people make heavy use of computers and digital devices, staring at the screen in front of them for 7-8 hours at a stretch; excessive concentration unconsciously reduces the number of blinks, so the eyes cannot be supplied with enough tear moisture and become dry.

Modern people often work overtime rushing projects and stay up late at the computer, remain long-term in environments with too little humidity (for example: air-conditioned rooms), which accelerates the evaporation of tears in a drying environment, or wear contact lenses — all of which make the eyes dry.

Age is a major factor in dry eyes: in anyone over 50, the state of ocular dryness grows progressively worse. Certain diseases such as thyroid disease, diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, and Sjogren's syndrome may also lead to reduced tear secretion.

Most of the time, dry eyes improve simply by blinking to produce tears, or after instilling clean normal saline. Applying warm compresses to the eyes, using a humidifier to correct indoor dryness, drinking more water to replenish fluids, resting more, and using an air purifier to reduce airborne dust or pollution can all bring improvement.

Severe dry eye syndrome is discussed in another article. For those whose eye use is not heavy yet whose ocular dryness has no identifiable cause, this is exactly where Chinese medical theory is best suited to provide an explanation and a new line of thinking.

records.etiology_en:
Dry, rough eyes are a symptom the ancients already had a thousand years ago. Antiquity had no such term as 'dry eye syndrome,' but it did have the term 'dry and rough eyes' (mu gan se). The Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic records it under the name 'despoliation of Essence' (duo jing); the Zhu Bing Yuan Hou Lun states 'when the humors are exhausted, the eyes are rough'; the Zheng Zhi Zhun Sheng mentions 'dryness, roughness, and blurred vision,' and so on.

Traditional Chinese medicine holds that the main cause of dry eyes is 'Yin depletion and Blood Deficiency,' for the Inner Classic speaks of the 'damage of the five taxations,' and the first of these is 'prolonged use of the eyes damages the Blood.'

So when a person's body is Blood Deficient, dry eyes readily appear. Chinese medicine further speaks of concepts such as 'the Liver stores the Blood,' 'the Liver opens into the eyes,' 'the Spleen manages the Blood,' 'the Heart governs the Blood,' and so on; dry eyes are therefore closely related to the Heart, Spleen, and Liver of Chinese medicine.

The tears of the eyes also belong to the fluids (jin-ye) spoken of in Chinese medicine; when a person's body is 'Dry-Hot,' insufficiency of fluids appears, and hence the eyes become dry and itchy.

All of the content above will have been seen by anyone with even a slight interest in Chinese medicine — utterly uniform, cliched, abstract, and offering nothing new, read without being understood. Is it not so?

If the causes of dry eyes could be detected with instruments and understood through data-driven analysis, more modern people would be convinced — and meridian testing can achieve exactly this purpose.

The analysis above belongs to 'zang-fu pattern differentiation,' while meridian testing belongs to 'meridian pattern differentiation.' To analyze diseases of the eye, one must first ask: which meridians lead to the eyes? According to the meridian authority Lin Yun-Gui's Illustrated Guide to the Meridians, fully 15 channels lead to the eyes (Note 1).

Summarizing these meridians, the principal ones are the Liver, Heart, Gallbladder, Stomach, Small Intestine, Triple Burner, and Bladder channels. How exactly do these abstract meridians affect the eyes and produce dryness?

From long-term observation of some Cloud TCM members, it emerges that the meridian phenomena shaping dry eyes can be divided into the following 3 steps:

Step 1: Fatigue shapes Liver channel Excess and Gallbladder channel abnormality

In anyone who regularly stays up late, is under heavy stress, and accumulates fatigue — regardless of whether the eyes are heavily used — the Liver channel in the body has a very high probability of beginning to show Excess. In most people the Gallbladder channel is long-term Deficient; in habitual night-owls, the Gallbladder channel converts to Excess.

After staying up late and excessive fatigue, the Liver and Gallbladder channels begin to become abnormal.

On this basis, in anyone who regularly stays up late, the Liver and Gallbladder channels become distinctly abnormal, presenting a phenomenon of meridian imbalance; and in the Five Phases these two channels belong precisely to 'Wood.'

Step 2: Spleen and Bladder channel Deficiency

A very particular phenomenon of the body's meridians is that when a person's Liver channel is Excess, the Spleen and Bladder channels begin to turn Deficient. The Bladder channel originates precisely at the eyes; when the body's Spleen channel is Deficient, the clear Yang Qi bound for the face suffers insufficient Qi and Blood, and the eyes begin to develop a dry, gritty sensation.

After Liver channel Excess, the energy of the Spleen and Bladder channels drops rapidly.

In the Five Phases the Spleen-Stomach belongs to 'Earth'; when Wood in the body is strong it overcontrols Earth, so the Spleen-Stomach weakens. This is why heavy eyelids or photophobia appear when the eyes are dry: people with Spleen channel Deficiency very readily develop all kinds of eyelid symptoms, and eyes with insufficient Qi and Blood very readily fear light.

Step 3: Triple Burner, Large Intestine, and Stomach channel Excess

The two processes above constitute the typical 'Iron Triangle meridian pattern.' Once this pattern has persisted for a time, the phenomenon of Triple Burner, Large Intestine, and Stomach channel Excess appears, and a series of Fire-Heat symptoms begins inside the body — hence the eyes become itchy and red, with dry mouth and tongue. This is the classic phenomenon of 'Liver Qi stagnation transforming into Heat,' which can now be seen clearly through data.

Internal Fire begins to appear.

This is why dry eyes are usually accompanied by redness, burning, dry itching, and foreign-body sensation — all produced by these meridian abnormalities.

By the meridian phenomena of Step 3, these are the phenomena almost all people over 50 show long-term; so it is only natural that a person past 50 develops dry eyes.

Based on the analysis above, to truly improve the phenomenon of dry eyes one must operate in reverse, following these steps:

Sleep one's fill and release accumulated fatigue: the Liver and Gallbladder channels then naturally return to normal, the Spleen and Bladder channels do not become Deficient, and the transformation-into-Heat phenomenon does not appear.

Pat the meridians and eliminate channel-sinew adhesions: judging from the meridian phenomena above, one should at minimum regularly pat the Spleen, Bladder, and Gallbladder channels to unblock the Qi and Blood of these meridians. At times one must use grasping-and-pinching methods to locate trigger points around the head, shoulders, and back; see the information below.

Take Chinese herbs or foods: pairing this with some Chinese herbs or foods that 'harmonize the Liver and Spleen' and 'nourish the Blood and the Liver' will naturally help to a certain degree. If internal Fire is strong, add some Heat-clearing, toxin-resolving herbs for an even greater supportive effect.

The analysis above proceeds from the meridian phenomena produced by 'lifestyle habits.' However, when autumn and winter arrive and external Cold produces Deficiency of the three leg-Yang channels (Bladder, Gallbladder, and Stomach channels), dry eyes also readily appear — this is yet another meridian phenomenon that produces ocular dryness.

Judging from the meridian-constitution data of large numbers of modern people, modern people in fact very readily develop dry, tired, and painful eyes; simply by regularly cultivating health, understanding, and improving one's own 'meridian constitution,' this symptom can be improved at the root.

Note 1: The meridians leading to the eyes are the Liver channel, the Liver divergent luo, the Heart channel, the Heart luo-vessel, the Heart divergent channel, the Gallbladder channel, the Gallbladder divergent channel, the Stomach channel, the Stomach divergent channel, the Yang Qiao vessel, the Yin Qiao vessel, the Ren (Conception) vessel, the Small Intestine channel, the Triple Burner channel, and the Bladder channel.

records.etiology_zh:
咽喉有異物感，是困擾中國人千年以上的老毛病。早在古代，就有對此症狀的記載。

《金匱要略》中形容為「咽中如有炙臠」，即咽喉彷彿卡著烤肉塊；《古今醫鑒》則稱之為「梅核氣」，形象地描述了那種「咯之不出、咽之不下」的異物感。

傳統中醫認為，「咽喉有異物感」屬於「鬱證」範疇，多因情志不舒、氣機阻滯所致。

古人認為，情緒是導致咽喉有異物感的主要原因

也就是說，古人早已將這種症狀歸因於情緒因素。最常見的證型是「肝氣鬱結、痰氣互結」。

典型表現為：異物感明顯，情緒波動時加重，伴隨胸悶脅脹、善太息、抑鬱易怒，舌淡紅、苔薄白或白膩，脈多弦滑。

根據《黃帝內經》的描述，肝經的支脈穿過橫膈、注入肺部，其主幹則沿著咽喉後方上行至鼻咽，再與眼目相連，上達頭頂。

這樣的經絡分布使得肝氣失調時，容易影響咽喉，產生異物感（梅核氣）。

當肝的疏洩功能受阻、氣機運行不暢時，初期常表現為胸悶、肋痛、容易嘆氣。

若氣滯持續3至6個月，就可能出現咽喉不適的情況。若氣滯長達一年以上，則容易進一步發展為「痰氣互結」的狀態——由於津液代謝失調，產生無形之痰。

進一步來說，這種「痰氣互結」往往伴隨「脾虛痰濕」。患者不僅有咽喉黏痰感，還常見體倦乏力、食慾不振、大便溏軟等症狀，舌淡胖、有齒痕，苔白膩，脈象濡滑。

這是因脾虛生濕，濕聚成痰，進一步阻塞氣道所導致的。

以上講的只是理論，實際上是怎麼樣呢？從雲端中醫數百個「咽喉有異物感」的經絡型態中發現，60%以上都屬於「綜合經絡型態」與「鐵三角經絡型態」。

這兩種經絡型態的交集點，就是肝經實證、脾經虛證。其中「鐵三角經絡化火熱極致型態」竟然高達45%以上，這就是典型與情緒壓力及鬱悶有關的經絡型態，完全印證古代中醫理論。

最常出現梅核氣的兩種經絡型態

由於這種經絡型態，都可能長達數十年以上，因此有一定比例的人就會出現「痰氣互結」，自然出現咽喉有異物感。

改善的方法也很單純，就是運用中藥疏肝理氣、健脾化痰、理氣和中，就可以快速改善，最常運用的中藥是「半夏厚朴湯」

平時可以經常按摩太衝穴、內關穴、膻中穴，這可以疏肝理氣。配合足三里、豐隆穴、陰陵泉穴化痰散結。三陰交穴、照海穴滋陰降火，就可以加速痊癒。

此外，傳統中醫也認為陰虛火旺時也會造成咽喉有異物感，因為腎經也通過咽喉，虛火上炎時咽喉乾澀灼熱，異物感伴口乾、心煩失眠、手足心熱，舌紅少苔，脈細數。

由於肺經、心經也通過咽喉，所以心肝鬱熱、肺部火熱，氣鬱化火時，會出現咽喉灼痛、異物感明顯，急躁易怒、口苦口乾、失眠多夢，舌紅苔黃，脈弦數。

事實上，「鐵三角經絡化火熱極致型態」的腎經普遍虛證，有些人會轉成實證，這就是一種陰虛火旺的現象。

火熱的肺經、三焦經、大腸經實證，會導致整個胸部火熱，出現心火、肺火，因此咽喉會感到很不舒服。

中醫認為，咽喉有異物感，通常與情志相關，治療需身心同調，不能只有依賴藥物。

平時必須保持情緒舒暢，避免壓抑或焦慮，可練習深呼吸、冥想。飲食忌辛辣、油炸、冷飲及過甜食物；痰濕者少食肥甘厚味，才能根本預防與治療。

有一部分人會出現咽喉異物感，但這種感覺對多數人來說難以理解。造成這種現象的原因很多，常見的包括：慢性咽喉炎、胃食道逆流、心理壓力，或其他結構上的異常。

治療方式則因人而異，常見的方法包括：藥物治療（如抑制胃酸、抗憂鬱藥）、改善生活習慣（避免辛辣食物、戒菸）、心理輔導與放鬆練習，以及定期檢查（如喉鏡、胃鏡），以排除潛在的嚴重疾病。

除了這些可以檢查出來的原因之外，從中醫經絡的角度來看，這種症狀也能獲得合理解釋，而且經適當調理後，改善的機率相當高。

Some people experience a foreign-body sensation in the throat, a feeling that is difficult for most people to understand. There are many causes of this phenomenon; common ones include: chronic pharyngolaryngitis, gastroesophageal reflux, psychological stress, or other structural abnormalities.

Treatment varies from person to person; common approaches include: medication (such as gastric acid suppression, antidepressants), improvement of lifestyle habits (avoiding spicy foods, quitting smoking), psychological counseling and relaxation exercises, and regular examinations (such as laryngoscopy and gastroscopy) to rule out potentially serious underlying disease.

Beyond these causes that can be identified by examination, from the perspective of the Chinese medical meridians this symptom can also be reasonably explained, and with appropriate conditioning the probability of improvement is quite high.

records.etiology_en:
A foreign-body sensation in the throat is an old complaint that has troubled the Chinese for more than a thousand years. Records of this symptom exist from early antiquity.

The Jin Gui Yao Lue (Essentials from the Golden Cabinet) describes it as 'a feeling in the throat as if a piece of roasted meat were lodged there'; the Gu Jin Yi Jian (Medical Mirror Ancient and Modern) calls it 'plum-pit Qi' (mei he qi), vividly depicting that foreign-body sensation which 'can neither be coughed out nor swallowed down.'

Traditional Chinese medicine assigns 'foreign-body sensation in the throat' to the category of 'constraint patterns' (yu zheng), mostly caused by emotional discontent and obstruction of the Qi dynamic.

The ancients held that emotions are the main cause of the foreign-body sensation in the throat.

That is to say, the ancients had long since attributed this symptom to emotional factors. The most common pattern is 'Liver Qi stagnation with Phlegm and Qi mutually binding.'

The typical presentation is: a pronounced foreign-body sensation, aggravated during emotional fluctuations, accompanied by chest oppression and hypochondriac distension, frequent sighing, and depression with irritability; the tongue is pale red with a thin white or white greasy coating, and the pulse is mostly wiry and slippery.

According to the description in the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic, a branch of the Liver channel passes through the diaphragm and pours into the Lung, while its main course ascends along the back of the throat to the nasopharynx, then connects with the eyes and reaches up to the vertex.

This channel distribution means that when Liver Qi is disordered, it easily affects the throat and produces the foreign-body sensation (plum-pit Qi).

When the Liver's free-coursing function is impeded and the movement of the Qi dynamic is not smooth, the early stage commonly manifests as chest oppression, rib-side pain, and a tendency to sigh.

If the Qi stagnation persists for 3 to 6 months, throat discomfort may appear. If the Qi stagnation lasts a year or more, it readily develops further into the state of 'Phlegm and Qi mutually binding' — formless Phlegm produced by disordered fluid metabolism.

Going further, this 'Phlegm-Qi mutual binding' is often accompanied by 'Spleen Deficiency with Phlegm-Damp.' Patients not only have a sensation of sticky phlegm in the throat but also commonly show fatigue and lack of strength, poor appetite, and loose, soft stools; the tongue is pale and swollen with tooth marks and a white greasy coating, and the pulse is soggy and slippery.

This is caused by Spleen Deficiency generating Dampness, the Dampness gathering into Phlegm, and the Phlegm further obstructing the airway.

All of the above is only theory — what is it like in practice? From the several hundred meridian patterns of 'foreign-body sensation in the throat' at Cloud TCM, it emerges that over 60% belong to the 'composite meridian pattern' and the 'Iron Triangle meridian pattern.'

The point of intersection of these two meridian patterns is Liver channel Excess with Spleen channel Deficiency. Among them, the 'Iron Triangle pattern transformed into extreme Fire-Heat' reaches as high as 45% or more — this is the classic meridian pattern associated with emotional stress and depressed mood, fully corroborating ancient Chinese medical theory.

The two meridian patterns in which plum-pit Qi most commonly appears.

Since these meridian patterns may persist for decades or more, a certain proportion of people develop 'Phlegm-Qi mutual binding' and naturally experience the foreign-body sensation in the throat.

The method of improvement is likewise simple: use Chinese herbs to course the Liver and rectify Qi, fortify the Spleen and transform Phlegm, and rectify Qi and harmonize the middle, and rapid improvement follows; the most commonly used formula is Ban Xia Hou Po Tang (Pinellia and Magnolia Bark Decoction).

In daily life one can frequently massage Taichong (LR-3), Neiguan (PC-6), and Danzhong (CV-17), which course the Liver and rectify Qi. Combine these with Zusanli (ST-36), Fenglong (ST-40), and Yinlingquan (SP-9) to transform Phlegm and dissipate binding, and Sanyinjiao (SP-6) and Zhaohai (KI-6) to enrich Yin and direct Fire downward, and recovery can be accelerated.

In addition, traditional Chinese medicine also holds that Yin Deficiency with effulgent Fire can cause a foreign-body sensation in the throat, because the Kidney channel also passes through the throat: when Deficiency Fire flames upward, the throat is dry, rough, and burning, and the foreign-body sensation is accompanied by dry mouth, vexation and insomnia, and heat in the palms and soles, with a red tongue with scant coating and a thin, rapid pulse.

Since the Lung and Heart channels also pass through the throat, when there is constrained Heat of the Heart and Liver or Fire-Heat of the Lung, and constrained Qi transforms into Fire, there appears burning pain of the throat with a pronounced foreign-body sensation, impatience and irritability, bitter taste and dry mouth, and insomnia with profuse dreaming; the tongue is red with a yellow coating and the pulse wiry and rapid.

In fact, in the 'Iron Triangle pattern transformed into extreme Fire-Heat,' the Kidney channel is generally Deficient, but in some people it converts to Excess — this is a phenomenon of Yin Deficiency with effulgent Fire.

Fire-Hot Excess of the Lung, Triple Burner, and Large Intestine channels causes the entire chest to become Fire-Hot, producing Heart Fire and Lung Fire, and hence the throat feels very uncomfortable.

Chinese medicine holds that a foreign-body sensation in the throat is usually related to the emotions, and treatment must regulate body and mind together — one cannot rely on medication alone.

In daily life one must keep the emotions relaxed and flowing, avoiding suppression or anxiety; deep breathing and meditation can be practiced. The diet should avoid spicy, fried, and chilled items and overly sweet foods; those with Phlegm-Damp should eat less rich, fatty, sweet, and heavy food — only then can prevention and treatment reach the root.

口中生瘡是一個困擾中國人千年以上的症狀，遠在《黃帝內經》就有提到，「口糜」、「口瘡」，或「口瘍」，類似的名詞非常多。

臨床上「口中生瘡」與「口角生瘡」是分開來討論，由於形成原因類似，這裡合併討論。

與其他症狀一樣，要探討口部的疾病，首先就是要先探討通往口部附近有哪些經絡？

通往口部附近的經絡相當多，包含大腸經、胃經、任督兩脈、心經別絡、沖脈、陰蹻脈、肝經。

由於良導絡經絡檢測的只有12經絡，因此口中生瘡及口角炎，最有可能就是大腸經、胃經、心經與肝經異常時所造成的現象。在實際觀察後發現果真如此，列述如下：

1. 季節性的現象：肝經與胃經實證

現代醫學常說，口腔潰瘍是體內免疫力不足的明顯訊號，所謂的免疫力不足，其實就是經絡「短期」或「長期」出現紊亂、不平衡的現象，只要經絡平衡之後就可以改善！

首先觀察肝經與胃經的經絡平衡指數，從下圖可以清楚看出，北半球每年到了3月之後，肝經與胃經的能量就開始增強，一直持續整個春夏，到了秋天之後才開始下降。

肝經與胃經的經絡平衡指數，在進入3月之後增高

這代表的訊息就是，這段期間出現口瘡、口角炎的機率大增。這裡可以舉個真實案例，某會員H小姐在進入2022年3月初的早晨，女兒向他抱怨口角長出一個痛痛的白泡泡，她對女兒說：「沒關係，這是火氣大！」

結果隔一天她早上起床之後，也發現自己的嘴角也長了一個白泡泡，這時候她開始覺得很納悶，怎麼會一模一樣呢？這症狀明顯出現在天氣變熱之後，上星期還處於濕冷的寒流呢！

晚上的時候，就把女兒抓過來進行經絡檢測，呈現下圖，從圖上可以明顯看到肝經與胃經實證。結果換她幫自己檢測，發現也是一樣出現肝經與胃經實證。

肝經與胃經實證，出現口角炎案例

為什麼現代醫學說，這通常只要1-2星期就會自動痊癒？這是因為這種肝經與胃經不平衡現象，身體也會自己調整，讓這兩條經絡自動回歸至正常狀態。

然而，有些人一年四季都是呈現這種經絡型態，這已經成為一種體質現象，這應該就是那些慢性口瘡、口角炎背後的一個原因！

2. 脾胃積熱：觀察陽明經(胃經與大腸經)實證與脾經虛證

延續上面的論述，從中醫理論來看，造成口瘡的另一個主要原因就是脾胃積熱，因此透過清熱瀉胃火可以改善口瘡。

這可以透過觀察陽明經(大腸經、胃經)，以及大腸經的表裡經[肺經]、胃經的表裡經[脾經]之間的關係來觀察經絡型態。

中醫說「脾之竅在口」，所以由於「脾喜燥惡濕」，而夏天就是濕氣重。從大量現代人的經絡數據看來(下圖)。

每年到了3-4月之後，這三條經絡能量產生巨大變化，陽明經能量提高，脾經開始出現嚴重虛證，這就有很大的機率會出現口腔潰瘍。

濕熱天氣下，陽明經實證，脾經虛證容易出現口腔潰瘍

傳統中醫認為，「脾胃積熱」容易出現口瘡，在口、唇、舌及齒齦多處生瘡，周圍紅腫，喜愛喝冰水、便秘、尿黃赤、身體發熱、舌質紅苔黃，脈數有力。

當這種經絡型態出現的時候，也會經常會感到口渴、大便秘結，尿色變黃，身體發熱，各位讀者都可以實際用自己的身體去驗證。

由於這種經絡現象通常在炎熱夏天出現，屬於神秘鐵三角經絡變化型的其中一種，由於大腸經也會影響到大腸，因此容易出現大腸相關的疾病。

現代醫學也發現，造成口腔潰瘍的腸胃疾病中，尤以克隆氏症及潰瘍性結腸炎為大宗，完為印證中醫的經絡理論。

當大腸經有熱時，基於表裡關係，會影響到肺經。肺經與大腸異常時，經常會造成皮膚相關疾病，現代醫學也發現，一些皮膚病如：扁平苔癬、天皰瘡…等，也常會出現口腔潰瘍。

某會員T小姐就曾經提到，她每次到了夏天時就容易出現口內發炎現象，她觀察自己的經絡就是呈現三焦經、大腸經、肝經、胃經實證。這種現象到了冬天就會自動消失，可見節氣對人體的影響是相當具大。

這時候服用瀉火的中藥可以改善口腔潰瘍，反過來看那如果經常食用辛辣(辣椒、胡椒)、油膩的食物(例如：麻辣鍋、五更腸旺…等等)。

又經常喝酒或喝咖啡，食用一些熱性食物(例如：牛肉、羊肉等、荔枝、榴槤…等等)，會增加體內的胃火，形成一種實熱，那就更難治癒了。

經常食用麻辣鍋，很容易出現口腔潰瘍

體內實熱的人一定要記得定時喝水，飲食清淡，無形之中就可以改善火氣症狀，改善飲食習慣就可以治病，不一定需要吃藥治病。[@ad:1]

 3. 心火旺造成口瘡：直接觀察心經、心包經

中醫說「心之竅在舌」，運用經絡檢測完全可以印證這句話！

雲端中醫某會員Y先生經常會觀察自己的身體，他發現2020年(庚子)在進入立春(2月)之後，就開始不明原因出現嘴破、口瘡，吃東西會痛。

而且經常口渴，感到很不舒服。有時候還潰感到胸悶、甚至胸痛，很擔心自己是不是受到病毒、細菌或黴菌感染。

去醫院檢查之後，醫生給了他一些外用藥膏還有一些抗生素，使用了之後有些改善，但是依然沒有根本治癒。

他對中醫科學化抱著濃厚的興趣，他非常好奇嘴破究竟是什麼經絡造成的？因此他連續三天都進行檢測，結果連續三天的經絡圖，都呈現心經、心包經實證的現象。

後來他運用Google 查了之後才知道，原來口瘡的成因到現在依然是個謎。而中醫古代典籍《諸病源候論》上記載：「手少陰，心之經也，其氣通受於舌；足太陰，脾之經也，其氣通於口。腑臟虛熱，氣乘心脾，津液竭燥，故令口舌乾焦也。」這句話是真的嗎？

運用經絡檢測快速證明瀉火中藥的效果

結果他自己馬上做了一個實驗，拿了一罐專門降火的「黃連解毒湯」來服用，服用後大約一小時之後再度檢測，心經與心包經竟然完全正常。

他才印證原來黃連降心火的速度這麼明顯！(註1)他告訴阿編說：「他真的嚇了一跳，中藥速度哪有這麼快？」這讓他覺得中醫真的在現代又重新活起來了！

讀過其他文章的讀者都知道，心火旺盛只是結果，造成火旺的原因還有很多，例如「陰虛火旺」、「心腎不交」，可以參考閱讀雲端中醫曾經探討心腎不交的文章(點選閱讀)。

任何人只要長期熬夜或睡眠障礙，就會造成「陰虛火旺」，而容易出現口瘡或口角炎。

多數亞洲人認為口腔潰瘍是體內火氣太旺所造成

4.、體內陽虛、中氣不足形成口瘡

以上所有論述，都是從實證、熱證的方向來思考，然而虛證有沒可能造成口瘡呢？還是有可能的。依照中醫理論，脾虛、氣血不足的人也會造成口瘡。

《景岳全書.口舌篇》中就指出，口舌生瘡這種病表面上看起來是上焦太熱所造成，可以透過服用寒涼中藥來治療。

但是有一種因為「中氣不足」造成的口瘡，這種一直吃寒涼藥是治不好的，反而要用熱藥(理中湯、附子)才能治癒(註2)。這一段話，可以運用現代經絡檢測加以印證。

上面提到心經實證的Y先生，其實不是第一次出現口瘡，過去7年間經常都會嘴破、口中生瘡，嘴巴附近永遠都會長痘痘，大約3年前開始幫自己經絡檢測，手三陽經經絡都是虛症。

每次他吃黃連解毒湯之後都會快速改善，但是沒多久口瘡又都長回來了，讓他感到很困擾。

長年反覆口瘡者，手三陽經虛證，心經心包經實證

他參考雲端中醫的相關文章，理解這是屬於「陽虛」的經絡現象，主要是「寒氣」或「濕氣」所造成。

住在台灣宜蘭的他證實，房間的相對濕度永遠都在90%以上，就算開了一整天除濕機，竟然相對濕度依然保持在85%，簡直就是濕到不行。

他說：「他長年頭暈、頭昏精神無法集中，尤其是體重瘦到只有45公斤！」

2020年9月進入秋天之後，這種現象更為明顯，讀理工的他堅信良導絡檢測法的穩定度，至少在他身上一直出現重複的經絡型態，而他的脾胃虛弱與口瘡也一持沒有明顯改善。大家眼中的他就是柔弱、精神萎靡的樣子，氣血能量明顯不足。

有一天，另一位會員向他分享自己的經驗，他說：「我以前也是這樣，後來持續服用附子理中湯後，竟然不再出現口瘡了」

他又說：「若不是因為經絡型態顯現明顯陽虛，我還真不敢吃呢？結果是真的好了，我是信了！」

從圖上可以清楚看到，當手三陽經虛證時，其實手三陰經反而是實證，因此會出現心經火熱的虛熱現象。

這也證明古代中醫所說的「甘溫除大熱」，就是透過改善腹部的氣血，透過補脾健胃來根本解除體內的火氣。

注意：謹慎服用瀉火中藥、寒涼食物

口腔潰瘍時，其實服用或塗抹西藥抗生素、消炎藥、抗菌劑效果很快。不少中藥也具備同樣的效果，主要都是苦寒藥物。

口舌生瘡時，服用電視上經常廣告的「XX解毒湯」或是口內噴「廣東XX粉」、「西瓜霜」…等等，之後1-2兩天內沒有太大效果，就要考慮停止了。

原因在於，這可能會讓口腔潰瘍更難被治癒，因為這種狀況可能不是火氣所造成的。反過來可能是脾胃虛寒、氣血不足所造成，服用苦寒藥物只會讓一切狀況更嚴重，甚至傷腎。

尤其是年老人、身體虛弱的人及慢性病患者，一定要顧護脾胃，不可因為體內有火氣症狀，就一直服用苦寒瀉火藥物。

許多長年反覆口瘡不癒者，如果透過經絡檢測確認是陽虛體質，反而不能食用太多生冷寒涼食物，只會讓口瘡更難治癒。

其他改善口瘡、口角炎的方法

1.改善生活習慣

以上提到的相關經絡，以肝經、胃經為例，雖然在進入春夏之後能量會自然增高，但是一年四季如果熬夜的話，就不受此限制！基於此，生活規律，作息正常，睡眠充足才是根本預防之道。

許多會員都發現，熬夜後明顯可以讓脾經虛證，肝經與胃經呈現實證，這只會讓口腔潰瘍更難被治癒。

因此熬夜晚睡容易造成口瘡，任何人若是不想要吃藥，卻想要根本治癒這種現象，其實只要堅持每天10點就寢，充足睡眠一段期間之後口瘡就會自然消失。

這足以解釋，為什麼現代醫學也發現，長期睡眠不足或過度勞累是口腔潰瘍反覆發作的常見誘因，免疫力降低是出現口瘡的根本原因！

2. 調整食物營養

現代人衣食無虞，表面上看起來應該不會缺乏營養。然而由於偏食及飲食習慣不同(例如：長期吃素或食用精緻食物)，依然會出現缺乏維生素或微量元素的現象，例如缺乏鋅、鐵、葉酸、維生素B12、維他命B2、維他命C、鐵質…等都會引發口角炎。

現代人因為過度忙碌，經常會忘記食用水果，這也是容易造成維生素不足的原因，可以經常食用酵素較多的水果。

例如：奇異果、木瓜、蘋果、香蕉…等。有些寒性水果甚至可以改善或治癒口瘡：柿子、桃子、西瓜、梨子…等等。

3. 善用蜂蜜及蜂膠

蜂蜜本身就具有清熱解毒、斂瘡的功效，外敷具有消腫止痛的作用，研究發現蜂蜜可以改善治療胃、十二指腸潰瘍。

口腔潰瘍的人可以用蜂蜜水漱口，每次漱口時讓蜂蜜水在口中停留幾分鐘效果會更好，口瘡反覆發作的人如果可以嘗試內服與外敷。

「蜂膠」是由蜜蜂分泌的蜂蠟、花粉、枝芽上的樹脂所混合而成的膠狀混和物，具有隔離細菌、病毒的作用。

它具有更多強大功效，其中一種就是改善口腔發炎，有益傷口復原。因此經常口瘡的人可以善用它的天然神奇力量來幫助自己。

4. 服用相關中藥

究竟中藥降火，改善口腔潰瘍效果如何？其實是非常好的！從雲端中醫的大數據的資料看來，多數亞洲人在Google搜尋的中藥，竟然全部都可以改善口腔潰瘍，感覺體內火氣太大的人，可能比想像中的還多！

大家都在搜尋什麼呢？答案是：「清胃散」、「甘露飲」、「清心蓮子飲」、「竹葉石膏湯」、「玉女煎」…等等，這類中藥都明顯指出現代人都有清除胃熱的強烈需求，運用大數據即可一目了然！[@formula:92]

有些人是因為體內便秘太嚴重，造成陽明經實火，可以透過瀉大腸的方法來改善口腔潰瘍，例如：大承氣湯、大柴胡湯就可以達到釜底抽薪的效果。

因為長期脾胃虛弱所造成的口瘡，可以服用「補中益氣湯」、「黃耆建中湯」大補脾氣，並助其升運，使氣血充足並能上榮，因為氣血虛而久不斂口的潰瘍得氣血濡養，自會收口而愈。

口瘡雖然是體內火氣太旺的象徵，然而造成火氣旺的原因卻完全不同。從根本找出原因，調整體內寒熱，平衡相關異常經絡之後，長年困擾的反覆口瘡現象就可以根本改善。

任何人如果出現口腔潰瘍，物必要在第一時間內加以改善，藉以預防更多可能的疾病。

註1 : 金元名醫張元素提出，黃連有六大功效，「瀉心臟火一也，去中焦濕熱二也，諸瘡必用三也，去風濕四也，赤眼暴發五也，止中部見血六也」。

註2: 原文：「口舌生瘡，固多由上焦之熱，治宜清火；然酒色、勞倦過度、脈虛而中氣不足者，又非寒涼可治，故雖久用清涼終不見效此當察其所由，或補心脾，或滋腎水；或以理中湯，或以蜜附子之類反而治之，方可痊癒。此寒熱之當辨也。」
records.western_pathology_zh:
許多人會在早上起床後不明原因出現口腔潰瘍，亞洲大部分的人都會直覺認為是「火氣大！」

口瘡又稱為「口瘡性口腔炎」，也就是口腔內軟組織潰瘍或稱為口腔潰瘍，常出現在舌頭、軟顎、嘴唇內側和雙頰內側。發炎處有白色圓點、紅色外緣的突起或難癒的傷口，也是一般人說的嘴破。

發生在口部的類似的現象還有「口角炎」，也就是俗稱的「臭嘴角」，是上下嘴唇交界處的急性或慢性發炎。最明顯的症狀為嘴唇的單側或兩側起水泡、潮紅、糜爛、結痂、脫屑或潰瘍等。

造成嘴破與口角炎的原因，現代醫學發現其病因非常多。例如：物理性或化學性損傷，微生物(病毒、細菌、黴菌)感染、藥物引發、 全身性疾病、癌症及其它不明原因病變…等等，口腔潰瘍可以說是許多疾病的共同訊號。

最常出現的原因是缺乏「維生素B2」所引起。由於缺乏維生素B2時，會影響到皮膚和細胞膜的完整性，所以經常會出現口腔、眼周和皮膚的發炎反應。

有些人長期反覆出現口腔潰瘍

經常反覆的口腔潰瘍，大部分都與體內的免疫系統有關，真正的原因不明? 可能是生活壓力較大、免疫缺陷所造成，由此會產生更多疾病的可能性。

雲端中醫有一篇討論到憂鬱症的成因，就提到皰疹病毒會造成口腔潰瘍，竟然也埋下了未來得到憂鬱症的潛在種子(點選閱讀)！

多數人的口腔潰瘍會在2週內會自動痊癒，並不用特別治療。只需要注意飲食與調整作息，運用止痛、抗炎殺菌藥物產生薄膜來覆蓋傷口，即可減輕疼痛。

像這種原因不明的疾病，現代醫學總是歸類於家族遺傳、精神壓力、荷爾蒙變化、食物過敏…等等。其實很適合運用中醫理論，從另一個角度來理解嘴破與口角炎，提供一條新的思路。

《證治準繩．口瘡》：「口瘡一曰熱，經云：少陽司天，火氣下臨，肺氣上從，口瘍是也；二曰寒，經云：歲金不及，炎火乃行，復則寒雨暴至，陰厥且格，陽反上行，病口瘡是也」。

《雜病源流犀燭．口齒唇舌病源流》：「臟府積熱則口糜。口糜者，口瘡糜爛也。心熱亦口，口瘡多赤；肺熱亦口糜，口瘡多白；膀胱移熱於小腸亦口糜；三焦火盛亦口麋；中焦氣不足，虛火上泛亦口穈；服涼藥不效，陰虧火泛亦口糜；內熱亦口糜。」
records.western_pathology_en:
Many people wake in the morning to find unexplained oral ulcers, and most people in Asia will instinctively assume: 'Excessive internal Fire!'

Mouth sores, also called 'aphthous stomatitis,' are ulcers of the soft tissue inside the mouth — that is, oral ulcers — commonly appearing on the tongue, the soft palate, the inner side of the lips, and the inner side of both cheeks. The inflamed site shows a raised lesion with a white round center and a red rim, or a wound that is slow to heal; this is what people commonly call a 'broken mouth.'

A similar phenomenon occurring at the mouth is 'angular cheilitis,' commonly known as 'sore mouth corners' — acute or chronic inflammation at the junction of the upper and lower lips. The most obvious symptoms are blisters, redness, erosion, crusting, desquamation, or ulceration on one or both sides of the lips.

As for the causes of mouth ulcers and angular cheilitis, modern medicine has found the etiology to be extremely varied. For example: physical or chemical injury, microbial infection (viruses, bacteria, fungi), drug-induced lesions, systemic diseases, cancer, and other lesions of unknown cause, and so on. Oral ulcers can be said to be a shared signal of many diseases.

The most common cause is deficiency of 'vitamin B2.' Because vitamin B2 deficiency affects the integrity of the skin and cell membranes, inflammatory reactions of the mouth, the area around the eyes, and the skin frequently appear.

Some people develop recurrent oral ulcers over the long term.

Frequently recurrent oral ulcers are mostly related to the body's immune system, the true cause being unclear — possibly produced by heavy life stress or immune deficiency, from which the possibility of further diseases may arise.

Cloud TCM has an article discussing the causes of depression which notes that herpes viruses cause oral ulcers — and may even plant a latent seed for developing depression in the future (click to read)!

Most people's oral ulcers heal spontaneously within 2 weeks and require no special treatment. One need only pay attention to diet and adjust one's routine, and use analgesic, anti-inflammatory, antibacterial medications that form a thin film to cover the wound, thereby reducing the pain.

Diseases of unknown cause such as this are always classified by modern medicine under familial heredity, psychological stress, hormonal changes, food allergy, and so on. They are in fact well suited to the application of Chinese medical theory, which understands mouth ulcers and angular cheilitis from another angle and provides a new line of thinking.

records.etiology_en:
Sores arising in the mouth are a symptom that has troubled the Chinese for more than a thousand years. As far back as the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic there are mentions of 'kou mi' (oral erosion), 'kou chuang' (mouth sores), and 'kou yang' (oral ulceration) — the similar terms are very numerous.

Clinically, 'sores in the mouth' and 'sores at the corners of the mouth' are discussed separately, but since their formative causes are similar, they are discussed together here.

As with other symptoms, to examine diseases of the mouth one must first examine which meridians lead to the area around the mouth.

The meridians leading to the area of the mouth are quite numerous, including the Large Intestine channel, the Stomach channel, the Ren and Du vessels, the Heart channel's divergent luo, the Chong vessel, the Yin Qiao vessel, and the Liver channel.

Since Ryodoraku meridian testing covers only the 12 channels, sores in the mouth and angular cheilitis are most likely phenomena produced when the Large Intestine, Stomach, Heart, and Liver channels are abnormal. Actual observation confirms that this is indeed so, set out as follows:

1. A seasonal phenomenon: Liver and Stomach channel Excess

Modern medicine often says that oral ulcers are a clear signal of insufficient immunity in the body; this so-called insufficient immunity is in fact a 'short-term' or 'long-term' phenomenon of derangement and imbalance of the meridians — once the meridians are balanced, improvement follows!

First observe the balance index of the Liver and Stomach channels. From the figure below one can clearly see that in the Northern Hemisphere, from March onward each year, the energy of the Liver and Stomach channels begins to strengthen, persisting through the whole spring and summer and beginning to decline only after autumn arrives.

The balance index of the Liver and Stomach channels rises after the start of March.

The message this conveys is that during this period the probability of mouth sores and angular cheilitis appearing rises sharply. A real case can be given here: in early March 2022, one morning the daughter of member Ms. H complained to her that a painful white blister had grown at the corner of her mouth. She told her daughter: 'It's nothing — just excess Fire!'

The next day, after getting up in the morning, she discovered that a white blister had grown at the corner of her own mouth as well. At this point she began to wonder: how could they be exactly the same? The symptom clearly appeared after the weather turned hot — the week before had still been in the midst of a damp, cold front!

That evening she brought her daughter over for meridian testing, shown in the figure below; from the chart one can clearly see Liver and Stomach channel Excess. When she then tested herself, she found she likewise showed Liver and Stomach channel Excess.

Liver and Stomach channel Excess: a case of angular cheilitis.

Why does modern medicine say this usually heals on its own within 1-2 weeks? It is because the body also self-adjusts this phenomenon of Liver-Stomach imbalance, letting these two channels automatically return to their normal state.

However, some people present this meridian pattern in all four seasons; it has already become a constitutional phenomenon, and this must be one of the reasons behind chronic mouth sores and angular cheilitis!

2. Accumulated Heat in the Spleen-Stomach: observing Yangming channel (Stomach and Large Intestine) Excess with Spleen channel Deficiency

Continuing the discussion above: from the standpoint of Chinese medical theory, another main cause of mouth sores is accumulated Heat in the Spleen-Stomach; hence clearing Heat and draining Stomach Fire can improve mouth sores.

This can be observed through the meridian pattern formed by the Yangming channels (Large Intestine and Stomach channels) together with their interior-exterior partners — the Lung channel (paired with the Large Intestine) and the Spleen channel (paired with the Stomach).

Chinese medicine says 'the orifice of the Spleen is the mouth,' and since 'the Spleen likes dryness and abhors Dampness,' while summer is precisely heavy with Dampness — this appears in the meridian data of large numbers of modern people (figure below).

Every year from March-April onward, these three channels undergo enormous changes in energy: the Yangming channels' energy rises while the Spleen channel begins to show severe Deficiency, and there is then a very high probability of oral ulcers appearing.

In hot, damp weather, Yangming Excess with Spleen channel Deficiency readily produces oral ulcers.

Traditional Chinese medicine holds that 'accumulated Heat in the Spleen-Stomach' readily produces mouth sores — sores arising at multiple sites in the mouth, on the lips, tongue, and gums, with red, swollen surroundings — with fondness for drinking iced water, constipation, dark yellow urine, generalized heat, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a rapid, forceful pulse.

When this meridian pattern appears, one also frequently feels thirst, has bound, constipated stools, yellowed urine, and body heat — every reader can actually verify this with their own body.

Since this meridian phenomenon usually appears in hot summer, it belongs to one of the variants of the mysterious Iron Triangle meridian pattern; and since the Large Intestine channel also affects the large intestine, diseases related to the large intestine readily appear.

Modern medicine has likewise found that among the gastrointestinal diseases causing oral ulcers, Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are the most prominent — fully corroborating the meridian theory of Chinese medicine.

When the Large Intestine channel has Heat, by the interior-exterior relationship it affects the Lung channel. When the Lung channel and Large Intestine are abnormal, skin-related diseases frequently result; modern medicine has also found that some skin diseases, such as lichen planus and pemphigus, often present with oral ulcers.

Member Ms. T once mentioned that every summer she readily develops inflammation inside the mouth; observing her own meridians, she presents Excess of the Triple Burner, Large Intestine, Liver, and Stomach channels. This phenomenon disappears on its own when winter comes — clearly the influence of the seasonal nodes on the human body is immense.

At such times, taking Fire-draining Chinese herbs can improve the oral ulcers. Seen the other way round: frequently eating spicy foods (chili, pepper) and greasy foods (for example: spicy hot pot, five-geng pork intestine stew, and so on),

together with frequent alcohol or coffee and Hot-natured foods (for example: beef, lamb, lychee, durian, and so on), increases the Stomach Fire within the body, forming a kind of Excess Heat — and then it becomes even harder to cure.

Frequent consumption of spicy hot pot very readily produces oral ulcers.

People with internal Excess Heat must remember to drink water at regular times and keep the diet light; imperceptibly, this improves the Fire symptoms — correcting one's dietary habits can itself treat the disease, and taking medicine is not always necessary. [@ad:1]

3. Exuberant Heart Fire causing mouth sores: directly observing the Heart and Pericardium channels

Chinese medicine says 'the orifice of the Heart is the tongue,' and meridian testing can fully corroborate this saying!

Cloud TCM member Mr. Y frequently observes his own body. He found that in 2020 (a gengzi year), after Lichun (the beginning of spring, February), he began to develop unexplained broken mouth and mouth sores, painful when eating.

He was also frequently thirsty and felt very uncomfortable, at times even experiencing chest oppression and chest pain, and worried whether he had been infected by a virus, bacteria, or fungus.

After examination at the hospital, the doctor gave him some topical ointments and some antibiotics; after using them there was some improvement, but still no fundamental cure.

Holding a keen interest in the scientization of Chinese medicine, he was very curious which meridians actually produce a broken mouth, so he tested himself for three consecutive days — and the meridian charts of all three days showed the phenomenon of Heart and Pericardium channel Excess.

Only later, after searching on Google, did he learn that the cause of mouth sores remains a mystery to this day. And the ancient Chinese medical text Zhu Bing Yuan Hou Lun records: 'The hand Shaoyin is the channel of the Heart; its Qi communicates with the tongue. The foot Taiyin is the channel of the Spleen; its Qi communicates with the mouth. When the fu and zang have Deficiency Heat, the Qi mounts the Heart and Spleen, the fluids are exhausted and dried, and so the mouth and tongue become dry and parched.' Is this saying true?

Using meridian testing to rapidly demonstrate the effect of Fire-draining Chinese herbs.

He immediately ran an experiment on himself: he took a bottle of Huang Lian Jie Du Tang (Coptis Toxin-Resolving Decoction), a formula dedicated to lowering Fire, and tested again about an hour after taking it — the Heart and Pericardium channels had become completely normal.

Only then did he verify how marked the speed of Huang Lian (Coptis) in lowering Heart Fire really is! (Note 1) He told the editor: 'I truly got a shock — how can Chinese herbs be this fast?' It made him feel that Chinese medicine has truly come back to life in the modern era!

Readers of other articles will know that exuberant Heart Fire is only the result; the causes of the exuberant Fire are many more, for example 'Yin Deficiency with effulgent Fire' and 'Heart-Kidney non-interaction' — see the Cloud TCM article that discussed Heart-Kidney non-interaction (click to read).

Anyone who long stays up late or has sleep disorders will develop 'Yin Deficiency with effulgent Fire' and readily develop mouth sores or angular cheilitis.

Most Asians believe oral ulcers are produced by excessive internal Fire.

4. Internal Yang Deficiency and Middle Qi insufficiency forming mouth sores

All the discussion above has proceeded from the direction of Excess patterns and Heat patterns; but can Deficiency patterns cause mouth sores? They still can. According to Chinese medical theory, people with Spleen Deficiency and insufficient Qi and Blood can also develop mouth sores.

The 'Mouth and Tongue' chapter of the Jing Yue Quan Shu (Complete Works of Jing-Yue) points out that sores of the mouth and tongue appear on the surface to be caused by excessive Heat in the Upper Burner and can be treated by taking cold-cool Chinese herbs.

But there is a kind of mouth sore caused by 'Middle Qi insufficiency,' which constant use of cold-cool drugs cannot cure; on the contrary, warm-hot medicines (Li Zhong Tang, Fu Zi) are needed to heal it (Note 2). This passage can be corroborated with modern meridian testing.

The Mr. Y of the Heart channel Excess case above was in fact not experiencing mouth sores for the first time: over the previous 7 years he had frequently had a broken mouth and sores in the mouth, with pimples perpetually growing around his mouth. About 3 years earlier he had begun testing his own meridians, and the three hand-Yang channels were all Deficient.

Each time he took Huang Lian Jie Du Tang he improved quickly, but before long the sores all grew back, which he found very troubling.

Chronic recurrent mouth sores: the three hand-Yang channels Deficient, the Heart and Pericardium channels Excess.

Consulting the related Cloud TCM articles, he understood that this belongs to the 'Yang-Deficient' meridian phenomenon, produced mainly by 'Cold' or 'Dampness.'

Living in Yilan, Taiwan, he confirmed that the relative humidity of his room never falls below 90%; even with the dehumidifier running for a whole day, the relative humidity astonishingly stays at 85% — damp beyond all remedy.

He said: 'I have had dizziness, lightheadedness, and inability to concentrate for years — and above all, my weight has fallen to only 45 kilograms!'

After autumn arrived in September 2020, this phenomenon became more pronounced. An engineering graduate, he firmly trusts the stability of the Ryodoraku testing method — at least in his own case the same meridian pattern kept appearing repeatedly — while his Spleen-Stomach weakness and mouth sores showed no clear improvement. In everyone's eyes he was the very image of frailty and listlessness, his Qi-Blood energy clearly insufficient.

One day, another member shared his own experience with him, saying: 'I used to be like that too; later, after continuing to take Fu Zi Li Zhong Tang (Aconite Center-Rectifying Decoction), the mouth sores astonishingly never appeared again.'

He added: 'Had the meridian pattern not shown clear Yang Deficiency, I would never have dared to take it — but the result is that I truly recovered, and I am convinced!'

From the chart one can clearly see that when the three hand-Yang channels are Deficient, the three hand-Yin channels are conversely Excess, and hence the Deficiency-Heat phenomenon of Heart channel Fire-Heat appears.

This also demonstrates what ancient Chinese medicine called 'sweet warmth eliminating great Heat': by improving the Qi and Blood of the abdomen — supplementing the Spleen and fortifying the Stomach — the body's Fire is resolved at the root.

Caution: take Fire-draining Chinese herbs and cold-cool foods with care

For oral ulcers, Western antibiotics, anti-inflammatory drugs, and antibacterial agents, taken or applied, in fact work very quickly. Quite a few Chinese medicines possess the same effect, mainly bitter-cold drugs.

When sores arise on the mouth and tongue, if taking the 'XX Jie Du Tang' frequently advertised on television, or spraying the mouth with 'Guangdong XX powder,' 'watermelon frost,' and the like, produces no great effect within 1-2 days, one should consider stopping.

The reason is that this may make the oral ulcers even harder to cure, because this situation may not be caused by Fire at all. It may conversely be caused by Spleen-Stomach Deficiency-Cold and insufficient Qi and Blood; taking bitter-cold drugs will only make everything worse, and may even damage the Kidney.

The elderly, the physically weak, and patients with chronic diseases in particular must protect the Spleen and Stomach, and must not keep taking bitter-cold Fire-draining drugs merely because Fire symptoms are present in the body.

For the many people whose mouth sores recur year after year without healing: if meridian testing confirms a Yang-Deficient constitution, they should on the contrary not eat much raw, cold, or cooling food — it will only make the mouth sores harder to cure.

Other methods of improving mouth sores and angular cheilitis

1. Improve lifestyle habits

Of the relevant meridians mentioned above, take the Liver and Stomach channels as an example: although their energy naturally rises after spring and summer arrive, staying up late in any season is not subject to this limit! On this basis, a regular life, a normal routine, and sufficient sleep are the fundamental means of prevention.

Many members have found that staying up late clearly produces Spleen channel Deficiency with the Liver and Stomach channels presenting Excess — which only makes oral ulcers harder to cure.

Hence staying up late readily causes mouth sores. Anyone who does not want to take medicine yet wants to cure this phenomenon at the root need only insist on going to bed at 10 p.m. every night; after a period of sufficient sleep, the mouth sores will disappear naturally.

This suffices to explain why modern medicine has also found that long-term sleep deprivation or excessive fatigue is a common trigger of recurrent oral ulcers — lowered immunity is the root cause of mouth sores!

2. Adjust dietary nutrition

Modern people lack for nothing in food and clothing, and on the surface should not be short of nutrition. Yet owing to picky eating and differing dietary habits (for example: long-term vegetarianism or eating refined foods), deficiencies of vitamins or trace elements can still appear — for example, deficiencies of zinc, iron, folate, vitamin B12, vitamin B2, vitamin C, iron, and so on can all trigger angular cheilitis.

Modern people, being excessively busy, often forget to eat fruit, which is another cause of vitamin insufficiency; one can regularly eat fruits rich in enzymes.

For example: kiwifruit, papaya, apple, banana, and so on. Some cold-natured fruits can even improve or cure mouth sores: persimmon, peach, watermelon, pear, and so on.

3. Make good use of honey and propolis

Honey itself has the effects of clearing Heat, resolving toxin, and closing sores; applied externally it reduces swelling and relieves pain. Research has found that honey can improve and treat gastric and duodenal ulcers.

People with oral ulcers can rinse the mouth with honey water; letting the honey water linger in the mouth for several minutes at each rinse works even better. Those with recurrent mouth sores can try both internal use and external application.

'Propolis' is a gum-like mixture of beeswax secreted by bees, pollen, and resins from twigs and buds, with the effect of sealing out bacteria and viruses.

It has many more powerful effects, one of which is improving oral inflammation and benefiting wound recovery. People with frequent mouth sores can therefore make good use of its natural, remarkable power to help themselves.

4. Take the relevant Chinese herbs

How effective are Fire-lowering Chinese herbs at improving oral ulcers? Extremely effective! From Cloud TCM's big-data records, the Chinese formulas most Googled by Asians can astonishingly all improve oral ulcers — people who feel their internal Fire is too strong may be more numerous than imagined!

What is everyone searching for? The answer: Qing Wei San (Stomach-Clearing Powder), Gan Lu Yin (Sweet Dew Beverage), Qing Xin Lian Zi Yin (Heart-Clearing Lotus Seed Beverage), Zhu Ye Shi Gao Tang (Lophatherum and Gypsum Decoction), Yu Nu Jian (Jade Lady Decoction), and so on — this class of formulas clearly indicates modern people's strong need to clear Stomach Heat, plain at a glance through big data! [@formula:92]

Some people have such severe internal constipation that Excess Fire of the Yangming channels forms; the method of draining the large intestine can then improve the oral ulcers — for example, Da Cheng Qi Tang (Major Order-the-Qi Decoction) and Da Chai Hu Tang (Major Bupleurum Decoction) achieve the effect of 'removing the firewood from beneath the cauldron.'

For mouth sores caused by long-term Spleen-Stomach weakness, one can take Bu Zhong Yi Qi Tang (Center-Supplementing Qi-Boosting Decoction) or Huang Qi Jian Zhong Tang (Astragalus Center-Fortifying Decoction) to greatly supplement Spleen Qi and assist its upward movement, so that Qi and Blood become sufficient and can nourish upward; ulcers that had long failed to close owing to Qi-Blood Deficiency, once they receive the nourishment of Qi and Blood, will close and heal of their own accord.

Though mouth sores are a symbol of excessive internal Fire, the causes producing that exuberant Fire differ entirely. Find the cause from the root, adjust the body's Cold and Heat, and balance the relevant abnormal meridians, and the long-troubling phenomenon of recurrent mouth sores can be fundamentally improved.

Anyone who develops oral ulcers must improve them at the earliest possible moment, thereby preventing further possible diseases.

Note 1: The Jin-Yuan master physician Zhang Yuan-Su proposed that Huang Lian (Coptis) has six great effects: 'draining the Fire of the Heart, first; removing Damp-Heat of the Middle Burner, second; indispensable for all sores, third; removing Wind-Damp, fourth; for sudden outbreaks of red eye, fifth; stopping bleeding of the middle region, sixth.'

Note 2: Original text: 'Sores of the mouth and tongue certainly arise mostly from Heat of the Upper Burner, and treatment should clear the Fire; yet in those with excess of wine and sex or overwork and fatigue, whose pulse is Deficient and whose Middle Qi is insufficient, cold-cool drugs cannot cure it; hence although clearing-cooling drugs are used for a long time, no effect is ever seen. Here one must examine the origin — either supplement the Heart and Spleen, or enrich Kidney Water; or use Li Zhong Tang, or honey-prepared Fu Zi and the like, treating paradoxically — only then can it be cured. This is the distinction of Cold and Heat that must be made.'

records.etiology_zh: 新冠後症候群屬中醫「疫病瘥後」、「虛勞」範疇，病機以邪去正傷為核心：溫熱疫毒經口鼻侵襲，耗氣傷陰，病後肺脾氣虛，故見久咳不已、氣短乏力、動則尤甚；疫毒傷陰，肺腎陰虛者，可見午後潮熱、盜汗、口乾咽燥；痰濕留戀未淨，阻於胸膈，則見胸悶、咳痰粘膩難出；病邪日久及心，心神失養，可見心悸、失眠、健忘、情緒低落等「腦霧」表現。臨床以肺脾氣虛、氣陰兩虛、痰濕戀肺、心脾兩虛為常見證型。
records.western_pathology_zh: 新冠後症候群（長新冠）指急性感染後症狀持續超過三個月，且無法以其他診斷解釋者。目前推測的病理機轉包括：持續性低度發炎反應與免疫調節失衡、微血管內皮功能障礙影響組織灌流、自主神經系統失調（姿勢性心搏過速症候群等）、部分證據顯示病毒蛋白或RNA可能於組織中持續存在或再活化、粒線體功能異常影響能量代謝，以及類自體免疫現象。常見表現包括長期疲勞、活動後症狀加劇（post-exertional malaise）、呼吸困難、認知功能障礙（腦霧）、嗅覺喪失及運動耐受度下降，症狀嚴重度與病程長短因人而異。

records.classical_references_zh:
《聖濟總錄．傷寒門》：「論曰傷寒喘，其證不一。有邪氣在表，表未解無汗而喘者；有邪氣在裡，汗出不惡寒，腹滿而喘者。有潮熱者。有心下有水而喘者。古人治之，亦各求其本。故在表者當汗，在裡者宜下，至於心下有水而喘，則又當利其小便也。

《症因脈治．喘症論》：「諸經皆令人喘，而多在肺胃二家。喘而咳逆嗽痰者，肺也；喘而嘔吐者，胃也」。

《症因脈治．外感喘》：「暑濕喘逆之症，煩悶口渴，喘息氣粗，多言身重，汗出身仍熟，此暑濕之喘症也」。

《症因脈治．內傷喘》：「食積喘逆之症，胸滿，胃痛腹痛，惡食飽悶，大便或結或溏，上氣喘逆，喘嘔噯氣，此食積喘逆症也」。

《景岳全書．喘促》：「關格之證為喘者，…其病必虛裡跳動而氣喘不已。此之喘狀多無咳嗽，但覺胸膈舂舂，似脹非脹，似非短，微勞則喘甚，多言亦喘甚，甚至通身振振，慌張不寧，此必情欲傷陰，以致元氣無根，孤陽離劇候也」。

《醫學正傳．哮喘》：「大抵哮以聲響名，喘以氣息言。夫喘促喉中如水雞聲者，謂之哮；氣促而連屬不能以息者，謂之喘。」

《景岳全書．喘促》謂：「氣喘之病，最為危候，治失其要，鮮不誤人，欲辨之者，亦惟二證而已。所謂二證者，一曰實喘，一曰虛喘也」

《臨證指南醫案．喘》云：「在肺為實，在腎為虛。」
records.etiology_en: Post-COVID syndrome falls within the TCM categories of "post-epidemic convalescence" and "taxation fatigue" (xu lao). The pathogenesis centers on the pathogen having departed while healthy qi remains injured: warm-heat epidemic toxin entering via the mouth and nose consumes qi and injures yin, so that after the illness lung-spleen qi deficiency presents as persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue that worsens with exertion. Where epidemic toxin has injured yin and lung-kidney yin deficiency results, afternoon tidal fever, night sweats, and dry mouth and throat may be seen. Where phlegm-dampness lingers unresolved and obstructs the chest, chest oppression and difficult-to-expectorate sticky phlegm appear. When the pathological process persists and extends to the heart, the heart spirit lacks nourishment, presenting as palpitations, insomnia, forgetfulness, and low mood — the pattern often described as "brain fog." Commonly seen clinical patterns include lung-spleen qi deficiency, combined qi-yin deficiency, lingering phlegm-dampness in the lung, and heart-spleen deficiency.
